absent: The early portion of offline_pages before watermark recomputation is not shown, including initial isolation, migration, cache suspension and the setting of failure reasons.
Internals of watermark recomputation, fallback list rebuilding, rate limit adjustment, memory and node notification delivery, and firmware and architecture removal are not shown.
Numeric values, widths and padding for zone bounds, migratetypes, node states, frame numbers, orders and error outcomes are not shown.
Complete layouts for zone, page, folio, node and memory block descriptors beyond the fields touched here are not shown.
Behaviour of buddy list manipulation, order calculation, compound splitting, free page accounting, acceptance primitives and huge page migration checks beyond call sites is not shown.
Management of reclaim and compaction tasks, least recently used cache control, draining of all pages, threshold programming and per node task locking beyond the shown uses is not shown.
Handling of memory block devices, alternate maps, block registry updates, region release, spanned page accounting and node registration beyond the shown calls is not shown.
Alignment, online and validity helpers, undo and unset paths for isolation, section offline marking and trace emission details are not shown.
Timing, retry, concurrency, performance and failure rate characteristics beyond the shown locks and busy outcomes are not shown.
Exact diagnostic formats, warning thresholds and debug output side effects are not shown.

findings.text: The lane exposes processor cache control for a zone through zone_pcp_disable together with zone_pcp_enable and zone_pcp_reset. The first suspends caching, the second restores saved thresholds, and the third discards per processor state when the zone is empty.
The lane exposes zonestat draining through drain_zonestat. Callers pass a zone descriptor and a per processor statistics block and the routine folds outstanding differences into shared counters.
The lane exposes isolated range finalization through __offline_isolated_pages. Callers pass a frame interval and receive a count of frames newly taken offline, with already offline frames excluded.
The lane exposes range isolation through start_isolate_page_range. Callers pass a frame interval with an isolation mode and receive success or busy when unmovable content blocks progress.
The lane exposes isolation verification through test_pages_isolated. Callers pass a frame interval with a mode and learn whether every block is marked isolated and free of pinned content.

The lane exposes small helpers for movability classification, free page relocation for isolation, and acceptance of deferred pages through page_is_unmovable with pageblock_isolate_and_move_free_pages and accept_page.
The lane exposes memory hotplug completion and removal through offline_pages with remove_memory and __remove_memory plus node and thread teardown through try_offline_node and kswapd_stop.

Entry for completing a memory offlining attempt. On success it finalizes node state, quiets per processor caches when the zone empties, stops node services, announces completion and detaches the frame interval from the zone. On failure it unwinds isolation and reenables caches.

Entry for removing a physical interval. The locked form serializes against concurrent online activity while the unchecked form treats any failure to remove as fatal. Both require every block in the interval to be offline before proceeding.

Paired entries for preparing a frame interval for exclusive use. The first marks covering blocks as isolated after checking for unmovable content. The second confirms that marking persisted and that no pinned pages remain.

Entries for tearing down node level state. Node teardown proceeds only when no frames remain spanned and no blocks or processors still attach to the node. Thread teardown stops the node reclaim task exactly once and tolerates repeated calls.

Successful completion recomputes watermark minima first, then clears the normal memory node mark before the general memory mark when no normal frames remain, and marks the node memoryless before rebuilding fallback ordering. Per processor state is discarded only when the zone no longer holds populated frames, and background compaction and reclaim tasks are stopped with a removal announcement only when a valid node identifier was supplied.

Failure unwinds in reverse order of acquisition. Isolated framing is released, cancellation of the offline announcement is broadcast, cancellation of the node removal announcement follows when a node identifier was set, and processor caches plus least recently used handling are reenabled.

Suspending processor caching records no new thresholds and drains outstanding pages while holding a dedicated mutex. Restoring reinstates previously saved minimum maximum and batch values and releases that mutex. Discarding drains per processor statistical differences on every online processor before freeing per processor structures and reverting to shared boot time singletons, and it leaves boot time state untouched when already in use.

Draining folds each nonzero per processor difference into the corresponding shared zone counter and clears the source entry. Numa event differences are folded similarly when Numa support is present. Repeating the operation without new activity leaves shared state unchanged.

Finalization of an isolated interval walks from start to end under the zone lock after marking sections offline. Poisoned frames outside the buddy system are skipped, as are already offline frames with no references. Every other frame must be an unreferenced buddy block marked isolated, and each such block is detached from its free list with the walk advancing by block size. The reported result excludes already offline frames.

Range isolation operates at block granularity by aligning the requested interval outward to block boundaries. Edge blocks use a boundary aware helper that understands neighbors across the edge, while interior blocks use direct marking. A request contained in a single block marks only once. Any interior failure releases all blocks marked so far plus the trailing edge and reports busy.

Marking a single block isolated first accepts deferred content when present, then under the zone lock rejects blocks already marked isolated as a race. The unmovable scan is limited to the overlap between the requested interval and the block. Success relocates free pages for isolation and increments the isolated block count for the zone. Failure in offline mode reports the blocking page after releasing the lock.

The unmovable scan requires its interval to lie within one block. Contiguous memory allocator blocks are treated as movable only for allocator initiated isolation and as blocking otherwise. Other content is examined in order with the examiner allowed to skip whole buddy or compound extents.

Movability classification treats reserved frames as blocking, while nonreserved frames in the movable zone are accepted without further checks. Compound frames beyond the supported order are blocking, huge pages require migration support and list membership rules, and empty frames are accepted with buddy size skipping. Poisoned and offline frames are accepted only in offline mode, with offline acceptance relying on drivers to drop references during the going offline announcement. List membership or movable operations otherwise indicate movability and all remaining frames block.

Boundary isolation aligns its scan window down to the largest block size bounded below by the start of the zone. It verifies alignment, ensures all examined blocks share one zone, and honors a skip flag for already marked blocks. It returns immediately when the neighbor across the boundary is offline. It skips deferred extents and buddy extents with a warning if a buddy would cross the boundary, skips compound extents that end at or before the boundary or that are huge, and fails with restoration of the original type when a compound straddles the boundary.

Verification first waits for deferred huge page release, then checks that every valid block start carries the isolated mark, allowing for misalignment between block size and largest buddy size. It then holds the zone lock while scanning every frame for isolated status. The outcome is traced with start end and stopping position.

Acceptance of deferred pages removes a largest order block from list tracking, subtracts its size from free and unaccepted accounting, clears the deferred mark, releases the zone lock, performs the architecture acceptance without holding the lock, and finally returns the block to the buddy system at largest order to the tail. Redundant acceptance when the mark is already clear returns without further action.

Removal requires every block in the interval to be offline, records the owning node during that check, removes the firmware map entry, and brackets the remainder under a hotplug guard. Intervals without alternate maps remove devices then architecture metadata directly, while intervals with alternate maps use a dedicated path that requires all blocks or none to carry such maps. Conditional block registry removal and region release follow, with node teardown attempted when a node was identified.

Node teardown is skipped while the node still spans frames, including device memory, while any block still links to the node, or while any present processor still belongs to the node. Otherwise the node is marked offline and unregistered.

A dedicated batch mutex is acquired when suspending processor caching and released when restoring it. Suspension zeroes thresholds and drains pages while holding the mutex, and restoration reinstalls saved values before release. Discarding per processor state does not acquire or release this mutex in the shown code.

The zone lock in interrupt safe mode serializes marking blocks isolated, finalizing isolated intervals, accepting deferred pages, and verifying isolation. Marking uses scoped acquisition, finalization holds the lock across the whole walk, acceptance holds it until accounting completes then releases before architecture work, and verification holds it only for the frame scan.

Node reclaim task teardown serializes on a per node task lock that protects the task pointer. Physical removal serializes on a device hotplug lock in the locked entry form and brackets device and architecture work under a memory hotplug guard. Device removal under the device lock serves as a barrier against racing online attempts.

Diagnostic reporting for a blocking page and architecture acceptance of deferred memory both run without holding the zone lock. The former is deferred until after lock release to avoid diagnostic locking warnings, and the latter releases the lock before potentially lengthy acceptance work.

The zone descriptor holds synchronization and placement plus per processor state. It includes lock, zone_start_pfn, present and populated accounting, per_cpu_pageset with per_cpu_zonestats and their boot time singletons, saved thresholds pageset_high_min with pageset_high_max and pageset_batch, and a counter nr_isolate_pageblock for blocks under isolation.

The per processor statistics block contains vm_stat_diff sized by NR_VM_ZONE_STAT_ITEMS together with vm_numa_event sized by NR_VM_NUMA_EVENT_ITEMS when Numa support is present. Each entry holds a pending difference that draining folds into shared state and clears.

The memory block descriptor carries nid with state and start_section_nr plus an optional altmap pointer. The node descriptor carries an array of zones with present accounting and a reclaim task pointer kswapd.

Node memory presence moves from populated to memoryless through ordered clearing. The normal memory mark clears when no normal frames remain, then the general memory mark clears, both before fallback ordering is rebuilt. Failure paths restore the pre attempt announcement state through cancellation notifications.

Offlining announcements follow a success or cancellation pair. Success emits an offline completion after rate limit adjustment, while failure after isolation emits a cancellation. Node level removal similarly emits either last memory removed or cancellation of removal depending on outcome.

Block isolation moves from normal to isolated on successful marking with a per zone count increment, remains isolated while verified and finalized, and returns to normal on failure restoration or explicit undo. Already isolated blocks reject concurrent marking attempts as busy.

Processor caching moves from active to suspended while holding the batch mutex, then either back to active with restored thresholds on cancellation or to discarded with boot singletons when the zone empties. Deferred pages move from unaccepted largest blocks to accepted buddy blocks through accounting removal, unlock, architecture acceptance and tail insertion.

Physical removal moves from online required to firmware detached to device and architecture detached to registry and region released, with node teardown last. Alternate map presence requires an all or nothing decision across the interval, selecting either direct removal or the alternate map path.

Clearing node marks in the wrong order would expose a transient state where general memory is absent while normal memory appears present. Rebuilding fallback ordering before marking the node memoryless would leave the empty node visible to allocation fallback.

Finalization treats referenced frames, non buddy frames outside poison and offline allowances, and mismatched migratetype as fatal or warning conditions. Removing an interval with any online block is fatal in the unchecked entry, and partial alternate map coverage triggers a one time warning with an invalid argument result.

A compound page straddling an isolation boundary fails the attempt and restores the original type, with list membership or movable operations on such straddlers flagged as unexpected. Allocator blocks misclassified by mode, unaccepted extents skipped by largest size, and deferred huge page release without waiting would each cause false busy or missed isolation.

Emitting diagnostics while holding the zone lock risks locking warnings, so the blocking page is reported after release. Treating offline frames as movable relies on drivers dropping references during the going offline announcement, with later migration failing if references remain. Poisoned frames require mode aware leniency to avoid false blocking.
The upper bound for normal memory accounting is known as ZONE_NORMAL and the movable zone selector is known as ZONE_MOVABLE.
Node presence marks are known as N_MEMORY for general memory and N_NORMAL_MEMORY for normal memory.
Memory hotplug announcements are known as MEM_OFFLINE for completion and MEM_CANCEL_OFFLINE for cancellation, with block state MEM_OFFLINE indicating a block already offline.
Node removal announcements are known as NODE_REMOVED_LAST_MEMORY for success and NODE_CANCEL_REMOVING_LAST_MEMORY for cancellation, with NUMA_NO_NODE marking absence of an owning node.

Isolation and placement types are known as MIGRATE_ISOLATE for exclusive blocks and MIGRATE_MOVABLE for reclaimable placement, with isolation modes PB_ISOLATE_MODE_MEM_OFFLINE for offlining and PB_ISOLATE_MODE_CMA_ALLOC for allocator use.
Largest extent and memory sizing identities are known as MAX_ORDER_NR_PAGES with MAX_PAGE_ORDER and MAX_FOLIO_ORDER plus PAGE_SIZE for byte conversion.

Statistics and placement identities are known as NR_VM_ZONE_STAT_ITEMS with NR_VM_NUMA_EVENT_ITEMS and NR_UNACCEPTED plus FPI_TO_TAIL for tail insertion. Failure identities are known as EBUSY with EEXIST and EINVAL.

Build time selectors observed include CONFIG_ARCH_ENABLE_HUGEPAGE_MIGRATION for huge page movement, CONFIG_NUMA for Numa event accounting, and CONFIG_ARCH_KEEP_MEMBLOCK for conditional registry removal.
